# David Ouyang, MD

> Cardiologist and researcher building artificial intelligence for echocardiography. He is a physician-investigator in the Division of Research at Kaiser Permanente Northern California and an adjunct Assistant Professor at the Smidt Heart Institute at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center. His lab (the Ouyang Lab / EchoNet) develops, interprets, and deploys deep-learning models for cardiovascular imaging. He led the first blinded, randomized controlled trial of AI in cardiology and co-founded InVision Medical Technology, which builds FDA-cleared AI for echocardiography.

David Ouyang's research spans three pillars: AI model development (precision phenotyping from echocardiogram video), AI model understanding (interpretable medical AI), and AI model deployment (prospective clinical trials and health-system integration). His work has been published in Nature, Nature Medicine, NEJM AI, Circulation, JAMA Cardiology, and the European Heart Journal. He is the creator of the open-source EchoNet datasets and models (github.com/echonet), and his echocardiography models are FDA-cleared and deployed in routine clinical care. ORCID: 0000-0002-3813-7518.

## Frequently asked questions
- Who is David Ouyang? David Ouyang, MD, is a cardiologist and researcher building artificial intelligence for echocardiography, in the Division of Research at Kaiser Permanente Northern California and as an adjunct Assistant Professor at the Smidt Heart Institute at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center.
- What is he known for? Creating the open-source EchoNet datasets and models, leading the first blinded randomized controlled trial of AI in cardiology (Nature, 2023), and co-founding InVision Medical Technology, which builds FDA-cleared AI for echocardiography.
- What is EchoNet? A family of open-source echocardiography datasets and deep-learning models (EchoNet-Dynamic, EchoCLIP, EchoPrime) at github.com/echonet.
- Where did he train? BA in statistics at Rice University; MD at UCSF; internal medicine residency and cardiology fellowship; postdoc in computer science and biomedical data science at Stanford University.
- Is his AI used in clinical care? Yes — his echocardiography models are FDA-cleared and deployed in routine care; InVision's Precision LVEF (K232331, 2024) and Precision Cardiac Amyloid (K243866, 2025) are FDA 510(k)-cleared.
- How to contact or collaborate? Email david.ouyang@gmail.com.

## Research
- Mission: improve cardiovascular diagnosis and disease detection using computer vision and artificial intelligence.
- [EchoNet open datasets and code](https://github.com/echonet): open-source echocardiography datasets and deep-learning models used as a global benchmark.
- [Video-based AI for beat-to-beat assessment of cardiac function (EchoNet-Dynamic)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-020-2145-8): Nature, 2020.
- [Blinded, randomized controlled trial of sonographer vs. AI assessment of cardiac function](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-05947-3): Nature, 2023 — the first blinded randomized trial of AI in cardiology.
- [Vision–language foundation model for echocardiogram interpretation (EchoCLIP)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-024-02959-y): Nature Medicine, 2024.
- [Comprehensive echocardiogram evaluation with view-primed vision-language AI (EchoPrime)](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-025-09850-x): Nature, 2026.

## Clinical trials
- AI ECHO INSIGHT — Kaiser Permanente AI echocardiogram interpretation for systematic integration (Co-PI). ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07229300.
- ECHONET-LVH-RCT — blinded RCT of AI-guided precision assessment of wall thickness (PI). NCT05791227.
- ECHONET-SCREENING — AI-guided echocardiographic screening of rare diseases (Co-PI). NCT06664866.
- ECHONET-RCT — blinded RCT of sonographer vs. AI assessment of cardiac function (PI); published in Nature, 2023. NCT05140642.
- SCOUT ECHO-AI — screening cardiometabolic opportunities using echocardiography AI (PI). NCT07216859.

## InVision Medical Technology (co-founder)
- [InVision Medical Technology](https://invisionmedtech.com/): Y Combinator-backed company building FDA-cleared AI for echocardiography.
- Precision LVEF — FDA 510(k) cleared (2024, K232331); AI ejection-fraction measurement validated in a blinded, randomized trial.
- Precision Cardiac Amyloid — FDA 510(k) cleared (2025, K243866), with FDA Breakthrough Device designation (2024).
- Medicare New Technology Add-on Payment for Precision Cardiac Amyloid — up to $2,275 per inpatient stay, effective October 2026.
- Precision Cirrhosis — FDA Breakthrough Device designation for AI detection of end-stage liver disease from echocardiography.
